findings.summary: ok=True on satisfiable formulas: deleting a clause that implied a root literal keeps the literal but drops the clause from RAT candidates; both engines
failed_clause differs between engines when the failed step repeats a literal: native returns the step undeduplicated
valid proofs raise ValueError when a fresh variable index exceeds the formula's count plus the proof's length; both engines

not_checked: formulas and proofs past 10 variables, or long proofs of any kind
real solver proofs: every proof here is generated
the order RAT tries resolvents in: on a rejected RAT step the reference only bounds resolvents_checked, so that count is judged exactly only between the two engines
direct use of the Rust Checker and check_step: reached only through cdclkit_native.check_proof, plus the crate's own cargo test
headers declaring many more variables than used, and the Rust allocation abort rust/src/checker.rs documents
text parser edge cases, beyond one clause per line
CNF objects whose clauses were built without CNF.add, so repeated literals and tautologies in the input reach the checkers only after normalisation
drat-trim: not on PATH in this campaign, so nothing here compares with it
whether a root conflict should outlive the deletion of the clauses behind it: dratify does not document this, the reference assumes it does, as drat-trim does, and only ok=False would make it matter
